title: Turnpike: lightweight arch+seqlen-aware kernel autotuner and scheduler
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: our current kernel router picks implementations primarily by static model tags and coarse seqlen buckets. This leads to suboptimal latency/cost tradeoffs for mixed workloads (short-chat bursts + long-form prefill) across heterogeneous hardware.

Goal: build 'Turnpike' — a runtime component that recommends and gradually autotunes kernel choices per model-version + hardware fingerprint + seqlen trajectory. It must operate with a safety budget so production SLOs are preserved, and integrate with prefill/decode scheduling so kernel choices transition smoothly between phases of a request.

Key ideas: token-phase bucketing (early prefix vs decode), hardware fingerprinting (SM count, memory bandwidth proxy, compute capability), warmstart microbenchmarks from a shared catalogue, short online bandit explorer constrained by p99 and error-rate guards, and a fast rollback/fallback path when a kernel misbehaves. The component will expose recommendations to the existing runtime router and emit telemetry consumed by Console for visualization and rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Turnpike service can produce per model-version+hw fingerprint kernel recommendation within 2ms median decision latency
Safe exploration mode rolls out a new kernel on <=5% of traffic with automatic rollback if p95 latency increases by >10% or error-rate increases by >0.5%
Demonstrated 5-10% reduction in cost-per-token for mixed-seqlen workloads in canary compared to baseline, without measurable quality regressions
Integration with Console dashboard showing kernel choice distribution, per-kernel latency P50/P95/P99 and memory oversubscription events
rollout_plan: Phase 1: lab microbench harness + offline simulator (1 week). Phase 2: service + read-only recommendations to runtime for monitoring (2 weeks). Phase 3: safe canary (5% traffic) on non-critical models, monitor 72h, gradually increase to 25% if stable (2 weeks). Phase 4: full rollout with opt-in per-customer feature flag and Console controls for exploration budget (ongoing).
